Yes — that finishes it. I typed `"a weekend"` and only **A Weekend in Rome** stayed. **A Roman Holiday for the Weekend** dropped out even though it's got both "a" and "weekend" in it, because those words aren't sitting together as that phrase. That's exactly the distinction I wanted quotes to make.

And your assumptions match mine: needing the words next to each other and in that order is the whole point of using quotes, and capital letters still not mattering is right.

That was the last piece I'd been holding out for on search. Putting it all together — searching my titles, descriptions, notes and sources, ignoring capitals, filtering by label with `#`, combining with and/or/not and parentheses, and now exact phrases in quotes — search now feels complete to me. Nicely done. This one's good.
